title: Lifting Borel subgroups along quotients of connected algebraic groups
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A group is solvable if its successive scheme-theoretic derived subgroups eventually become trivial, where the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup. Let $G,H$ be smooth and connected and let $q:G\to H$ be a homomorphism such that $F[H]\to F[G]$ is faithfully flat, meaning that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. For every Borel subgroup $C\subseteq H$ there is a Borel subgroup $B\subseteq G$ such that $q|_B:B\to C$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Here finitely presented means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. No finiteness, centrality or multiplicative-type assumption is imposed on $\ker q$.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, printed pp.357--358, Borel assertion and its surjectivity onto the Borel subgroups of the quotient; Theorem 5.39, printed p.108, for the faithfully flat map onto the scheme-theoretic image, with its finite presentation as in lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-quotient-borel-torus-images] with $A=G$, $D=H$ and $f=q$. Its field, affineness, finite-type, smoothness, connectedness and coordinate-ring faithful-flatness hypotheses are exactly those here. Its assertion that every Borel subgroup of $D$ is an image gives a Borel $B\subseteq G$ with scheme-theoretic image $q(B)=C$. The same statement gives faithful flatness of $h=q|_B:B\to C$, in the coordinate-ring sense required here. The remaining issue is finite presentation, which is not asserted by that node.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, Borel-image assertion on printed p.357 and the conjugacy argument for prescribed Borels on p.358.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $h:B\to C$. These groups are affine of finite type by the hypotheses. They are separated: for an affine group with coordinate ring $R$, the diagonal is induced by the surjection $R\otimes_F R\to R$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, so it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], exactly the separatedness condition [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The factorization gives $B\xrightarrow{r}I\xrightarrow{i}C$, with $r$ faithfully flat and finitely presented and $i$ a closed immersion. Write $A=F[C]$, $S=F[B]$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $I=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ for an ideal $J$, and $A\to S$ factors through $A/J$. This map is injective directly from the faithful flatness obtained in step 1: if $a\in A$ maps to zero, tensor the inclusion $aA\hookrightarrow A$ with $S$. Exactness makes the resulting map injective, whereas it is zero because $a$ acts as zero on $S$. Hence $(aA)\otimes_A S=0$; detection of zero modules gives $aA=0$ and $a=0$. Thus $J=0$, so $i$ is an isomorphism over $C$. Identifying $I$ with $C$ in this way, $r$ is $h$. Its local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness therefore give precisely the finite presentation required. No property of $\ker q$ was used.

source.place: Theorem 5.39, printed p.108, and Remark 5.40 (uniqueness of the image factorization); elementary affine-ring verification that a faithfully flat homomorphism has full image.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 17.20, printed pp.357--358; Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.40, printed p.108. Assembly of existing general statements with the explicit affine-ring argument.
